events.title: Whirlwind magnetic core memory operational
events.summary: MIT's Whirlwind computer began using magnetic core memory in 1953 — the first reliable high-speed random-access memory for computers.
events.about: Jay Forrester's core memory array of tiny ferrite rings became the dominant RAM technology until semiconductor memory in the 1970s. Whirlwind itself was a real-time flight simulator for the Navy — core memory made fast, rewriteable storage practical at scale.

narrative.whyChosen: Magnetic core memory was the first practical high-speed RAM for digital computers.
narrative.whyImportant: It enabled fast, reliable storage that every mainframe and minicomputer adopted for two decades.
narrative.problemSolved: Earlier memory (delay lines, CRT stores) was too slow or unreliable for real-time computing.
